1.explanation: clients/devtools/devtools-entry.js is where DevTools forces screenEmulation.disabled=true. That flag flows into the core emulation description logic. lib/emulation.js implements getEmulationDescriptions(), which checks screenEmulation.disabled and, if true, returns the “no emulation” string. Together, these two files cause the DevTools UI to incorrectly label mobile runs as having no emulation.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse from within Chrome DevTools, DevTools sets screen emulation as disabled in devtools-entry.js. As a result, the shared getEmulationDescriptions() routine (in lib/emulation.js) sees screenEmulation.disabled===true and returns “No emulation” for the device description. The UI then shows “No emulation with Lighthouse” (as seen in the screenshot) even though a mobile emulation profile and CPU throttling are in effect.

2.explanation:
• clients/devtools/devtools-entry.js explicitly sets disableDeviceEmulation (maps to settings.screenEmulation.disabled) so that Lighthouse itself doesn’t try to emulate a device when DevTools is already doing so.  That flag is now causing getEmulationDescriptions to report “no emulation.”
• lib/emulation.js (which implements getEmulationDescriptions) returns the “No emulation with Lighthouse” string whenever screenEmulation.disabled is true.  It needs to special-case DevTools or use a different flag so that DevTools emulation still appears in the UI.
• third-party/devtools-tests/e2e/lighthouse/devtools-settings_test.ts contains the end-to-end assertion for the DevTools UI badge.  It’s now failing because the UI text has changed, so the test will need updating once the underlying logic is fixed.
2.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse from within Chrome DevTools on a mobile-emulated page, the UI badge and tooltip incorrectly say “No emulation with Lighthouse” instead of reflecting the DevTools device emulation.  In screenshot: even though DevTools is in mobile emulation mode (e.g. iPhone), Lighthouse thinks screen emulation has been disabled and shows “No emulation.”
